skill.name: aws-serverless
skill.description: Build and review AWS serverless applications using Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS, SAM, CDK, and production optimization patterns.
skill.summary: Practical guidance for AWS serverless architecture, implementation, deployment, reliability, and performance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit reviewed 126 static findings. One medium-risk finding is confirmed because an infrastructure example permits unrestricted IPv4 HTTPS egress. The remaining alerts are contextual false positives, and no malicious intent or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: The VPC security group example allows HTTPS egress to every IPv4 address.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict egress to required CIDR ranges, proxies, or VPC endpoints, and document when public internet access is necessary.

remediation.issue: API examples use wildcard CORS origins, methods, or headers.
remediation.suggestion: Use explicit production origins, methods, and headers. Explain that wildcard CORS is suitable only for intentionally public APIs.

remediation.issue: The CDK example sets DynamoDB removalPolicy to DESTROY.
remediation.suggestion: Default to RETAIN for persistent data and require an explicit development setting before enabling destructive removal.

semantic_findings.title: Overly Permissive CORS Examples
semantic_findings.description: Multiple API examples allow every origin, and the SAM example also allows every header. Production reuse can expose browser-accessible endpoints to untrusted origins.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Wildcard origin and header directives are explicit in three API examples. Impact depends on authentication and credential handling.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive DynamoDB Removal Policy
semantic_findings.description: The CDK example destroys its DynamoDB table when the resource is removed. A development-only comment helps, but production reuse could cause permanent data loss.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The removal policy is explicitly set to DESTROY. The nearby comment limits the intended context but does not enforce that boundary.

content.value_statement: AWS serverless systems require careful choices across compute, APIs, storage, messaging, deployment, and performance. This skill provides practical patterns for designing and reviewing production-focused architectures.
actual_capabilities: Creates Node.js and Python Lambda handler patterns with error handling and API Gateway responses.
Provides AWS SAM and CDK examples for APIs, functions, tables, queues, and permissions.
Explains HTTP API and REST API tradeoffs for Lambda-backed services.
Designs SQS and DynamoDB Streams processing with retries, dead-letter queues, and partial batch failures.
Recommends cold-start, memory, timeout, package-size, and concurrency optimizations.
Covers VPC networking, presigned S3 transfers, payload limits, and recursive invocation controls.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not inspect or deploy to an AWS account.
Resource names, regions, permissions, CORS rules, and network controls require environment-specific review.
Examples are starting points and do not replace testing, threat modeling, or cost validation.
AWS pricing, limits, runtimes, and service behavior can change after publication.

use_cases.title: Create a Serverless API
use_cases.description: Plan Lambda handlers, API Gateway routes, DynamoDB access, responses, and deployment resources for a new service.

use_cases.title: Design Reliable Event Processing
use_cases.description: Review SQS or DynamoDB Streams workflows for retries, idempotency, dead-letter handling, and batch failures.

use_cases.title: Optimize Production Lambda Workloads
use_cases.description: Assess cold starts, memory, timeouts, VPC access, payload limits, concurrency, and operational cost.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Lambda Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Node.js AWS Lambda handler for [task]. Include input validation, structured logging, API Gateway responses, and required environment variables.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner implementation for a single endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Design a SAM API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AWS SAM template for [API]. Use HTTP API, least-privilege DynamoDB access, configurable CORS, environment variables, and deployment outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate infrastructure design for a serverless API.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Event Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SQS or DynamoDB Streams workflow: [architecture]. Identify retry, idempotency, DLQ, timeout, batch failure, and observability improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reliability review for asynchronous processing.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Production System
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize this production serverless system: [details]. Compare memory, cold starts, VPC networking, concurrency, payload limits, cost, and failure controls.

output_examples.input: Design an SQS processing pattern for ten-message batches.
output: Use partial batch failure reporting so successful messages are not retried.
Set queue visibility timeout relative to function timeout and configure a dead-letter queue.
Make processing idempotent and monitor failed-message age.

output_examples.input: Review a latency-sensitive Lambda function attached to a VPC.
output: Measure initialization duration before changing memory or concurrency.
Use VPC endpoints for supported AWS services and restrict outbound network access.
Set explicit downstream timeouts and test cold behavior under realistic traffic.

output_examples.input: Plan uploads that exceed API Gateway payload limits.
output: Return a short-lived S3 presigned upload URL from the API.
Validate object size, content type, ownership, and key prefix after upload.
Keep large file bytes outside API Gateway and Lambda responses.

best_practices: Measure latency, memory, initialization time, and cost before changing Lambda configuration.
Use least-privilege IAM, restricted CORS, controlled egress, and environment-specific deployment settings.
Design event handlers for retries through idempotency, dead-letter queues, and partial batch failure reporting.
anti_patterns: Do not copy wildcard CORS, broad network egress, or destructive removal policies into production.
Do not process large files entirely in memory or route large payloads through API Gateway.
Do not deploy event consumers without timeout alignment, retry limits, idempotency, and failure monitoring.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation and infrastructure patterns that require review and execution in your environment.

faq.question: Which languages and tools are covered?
faq.answer: It includes Node.js, Python, AWS SAM, and TypeScript CDK examples, plus Java and .NET SnapStart guidance.

faq.question: Should I use AWS SAM or AWS CDK?
faq.answer: Use SAM for focused serverless templates. Use CDK when reusable constructs or broader infrastructure logic are important.

faq.question: Are the examples production-ready without changes?
faq.answer: No. Adapt permissions, CORS, network rules, retention settings, resource names, monitoring, and tests before production deployment.

faq.question: How should AWS credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use IAM roles and temporary credentials. Store application secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or another approved secret store.

faq.question: Does the skill cover other cloud providers?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on AWS and identifies separate specialists for comparable Google Cloud or Azure work.
